annotations.text:
THE HOOD

Chrome drops to three chunky buttons plus the drawer peek. Every icon is drawn, not emoji — emoji render differently per OS and sit badly next to hand-authored sprites.

The badge on Cat-a-log is the only count on screen. It earns its place: it says a cat you have not met is waiting.

DECORATING DRAWER

Category tabs, because 25 goodies stopped fitting a flat tray somewhere around 12. Locked items show a PRICE but never an effect — publishing '+15%' turns choosing a goodie into arithmetic with one right answer.

The scene stays visible above, so you can see what you are decorating.

THE PAYOFF

Currently a plain white modal. This is the emotional beat of the whole loop, so it is framed like a field photograph.

'Came for the cat bed' is what makes decorating legible without ever quoting a spawn percentage.

CAT-A-LOG — SHIPPED

It used to list cats you already had, which is a database view. A collection game runs on the EMPTY slots: silhouettes of breeds you have not met are what make the next cat worth chasing.

No schema change was needed after all — breeds come from the local sprite library and cats already carry sprite_template_id, so the grouping is derived client-side.

One thing was cut: the 'Likes shelter' hint. Spawn chances come from item bonuses alone with no per-breed affinity, so it would have been a lie.

SHOP

Swatches now sit inside the card radius, every row shares one gutter, and the buy button carries the price rather than a separate badge.

'50 more paw points' replaces 'Not enough' — a shortfall tells you how close you are; a refusal tells you nothing.

Every colour and spacing value here already exists in src/theme.ts. What is new is the lip, the icon rule, and the five alignment rules.

The alignment rules are the direct answer to the buttons being out of line: it was four different failures, not four decisions.
